findings.title: canManage() grants manage on all groups when caller only has VIEW scope
findings.body: GroupPermissionsV2.canManage() returns true when hasPermission(null, VIEW, MANAGE) succeeds, i.e. a permission on the 'all groups' resource granting only the 'view' scope is enough. canManage() is used by GroupsResource.addTopLevelGroup (requireManage()) and by V1-inherited paths, so an admin granted only view on all groups can create top-level groups and perform other manage operations. The check should be hasPermission(null, MANAGE) only, mirroring canManage(GroupModel) which correctly checks just MANAGE. The matching javadoc in GroupPermissionEvaluator.canManage() ('VIEW or MANAGE groups') repeats the same mistake.

findings.title: getGroupIdsWithViewPermission returns authz resource IDs instead of group IDs and never finds per-group resources
findings.body: In V2 per-group resources are created by AdminPermissionsSchema.getOrCreateResource with name = group ID and no type set, so resourceStore.findByType(server, "Groups", ...) will not return them (it only returns the 'Groups' all-resource whose type was set in init). For whatever it does return, the callback passes groupResource.getId() (the authz resource UUID) to hasPermission(), which does resourceStore.findByName(server, groupId) — the lookup fails and silently falls back to all-groups evaluation — and then adds the resource UUID (not the group ID) to the returned set. UsersResource/BruteForceUsersResource put this set into session attribute UserModel.GROUPS to restrict the DB user search, so the returned values are meaningless as group IDs. Current tests pass only because the post-filter usersEvaluator::canView happens to compensate; the DB-level filter (and getUsersCount(realm, ..., groupIds)) is broken. Should use getName() and ensure per-group resources carry the resource type.

findings.title: All-groups fallback is skipped whenever any permission exists for the specific group
findings.body: hasPermission only falls back to the 'Groups' resource-type resource when no resource named after the group exists. Once any permission is created for a specific group (e.g. granting only manage-members), that group gets its own resource and subsequent checks for other scopes (view, manage, manage-membership) are evaluated solely against it; an existing all-groups permission granting those scopes is ignored. So adding a narrow per-group permission silently revokes broader all-groups grants for that group. Evaluation should consider both the specific resource and the resource-type resource (or document this as intended, with tests).

findings.title: getResourceName does not resolve display names for Groups resource type
findings.body: getResourceName special-cases only USERS (mapping the resource name, which is a user ID, to the username, and 'Users' to 'All users'). For the newly added GROUPS type the method falls through to resource.getDisplayName(), but group resources are created by getOrCreateResource with name = group ID and no display name, so permission listings for groups will show null/empty names instead of the group name (or 'All groups'). A GROUPS branch resolving the group by ID is needed.

findings.title: Wrong javadoc on requireManageMembers
findings.body: The javadoc for requireManageMembers(GroupModel) says it throws when canManageMembership(GroupModel) returns false, but the implementation checks canManageMembers(GroupModel). Also the javadoc of getGroupIdsWithViewPermission says '@return Stream of IDs' while the method returns a Set.

findings.title: testManageGroupMembership does not isolate the group MANAGE_MEMBERSHIP scope
findings.body: The test grants both the all-users manage-group-membership permission and the group manage-membership permission before asserting that joinGroup succeeds, so it would pass even if the group-side MANAGE_MEMBERSHIP check were missing or ignored. There is also no test for canManage()/requireManage() rejecting a caller who only has VIEW on all groups, which is exactly the case GroupPermissionsV2.canManage() currently gets wrong.
